brief: A new bridge over Breiðholtsbraut has opened, and repairs at Búrfellsvirkjun are nearing completion, lifting energy curtailments, while a historic single-family home in 101 Reykjavík was also sold. A fire broke out in the roof of an apartment block in Bryggjuhverfi, and emergency line issues continue to be a concern despite Australian acknowledgements of error. Economically, the Minister of Industries emphasized protecting Elkem's international competitiveness, and warnings were issued about the significant impact on living standards if the Euro were adopted. The terrorism case has concluded with no appeal from the State Prosecutor, while Icelandic authorities are being compelled to hear stories from corruption victims.

items.title: Lóðaþjónustan ehf. með lægsta tilboðið í yfirborðsfrágang á Ártúnshöfða
items.summary: Reykjavík City received five bids for surface finishing, road construction, and piping in the Ártúnshöfði development area. Lóðaþjónustan ehf. submitted the lowest bid, which was below the project's cost estimate. The city will now review the bids before selecting a contractor for this ongoing urban development project.
items.why_matters: This marks a step forward in the ongoing urban development of the Ártúnshöfði area.

items.title: Kári leggst gegn umsókn að Evrópusambandinu
items.summary: Prominent Icelandic figure Kári Stefánsson has publicly stated his opposition to Iceland's application to join the European Union. He expresses significant concerns about the EU's current state and believes a pragmatic assessment of national interests would lead him to vote against accession in a referendum. He notes that his stance could change if global circumstances evolve.
items.why_matters: Iceland's potential EU membership would have profound implications for its economy, sovereignty, and international relations.

items.title: Ný stjórn Landspítalans skipuð
items.summary: The Minister of Health has appointed a new board for Landspítalinn, Iceland's National University Hospital, for the next two years. The board, comprising individuals with diverse backgrounds in administration, healthcare, and academia, will be responsible for setting long-term strategy and overseeing the hospital's operations and financial planning.
items.why_matters: The new board will guide the strategic direction and operational oversight of Iceland's largest hospital, impacting healthcare services.

items.title: Hefði aldrei verið samþykkt í dag
items.summary: The article discusses the controversial Radisson Red hotel tower in Reykjavík, nearing completion, which an architect argues would never be approved under current planning laws. She criticizes the city's past zoning decisions that allowed for such a large building and the financial incentives for municipalities to grant extensive building permits. The architect believes the building does not fit its environment and highlights issues with outdated planning.
items.why_matters: This article highlights how past city planning decisions can lead to controversial large-scale developments and raises questions about the long-term impact of municipal planning policies.

items.title: „Værum duglegri að halda garðveislur ef veðrið væri til friðs“
items.summary: Singer and radio host Regína Ósk Óskarsdóttir shares details about her extensive outdoor living space at home. She and her husband have built and continuously improved a large deck with a hot tub, cold tub, and a sauna. They are also planning future additions like an outdoor kitchen and living room, even using AI for design ideas.

items.title: Einn stór turn í stað þriggja minni
items.summary: Construction is well underway on a large hotel tower at Skúlagata 26 in Reykjavik. An architect, who abstained from the 2015 planning council vote, points out that the current single large building consolidates the volume of three smaller towers originally planned for the site.
items.why_matters: This article details a significant change in a specific urban development project in Reykjavik, directly impacting the city's landscape.

items.title: Yfir hundrað í­búðir gjörskemmdar
items.summary: A large fire in Drammen, Norway, has destroyed over a hundred apartments and forced the evacuation of 400 residents. Firefighters are still battling the blaze, which the mayor has described as a disaster. Two people were hospitalized for smoke inhalation, and several emergency personnel were also affected.
items.why_matters: This major fire has displaced hundreds of people and caused extensive property damage in Norway.

items.title: 295 milljóna lúxushús við Álmakór
items.summary: This article features a 295 million ISK luxury house in Kópavogur, highlighting its unique design and prime location. It details the contributions of a team of architects and designers, including Sigurður Hallgrímsson for the house design and Guðbjörg Magnúsdóttir for interior design. The property boasts high-end features, spacious rooms, and extensive outdoor living areas.

items.title: Mun ekki láta lögreglu ráðast gegn netsölu áfengis
items.summary: The Justice Minister, Þorbjörg Sigríður Gunnlaugsdóttir, has stated she will not order the police to take specific action against online alcohol retailers. This decision comes despite a recent district court ruling against an online seller, as the case is currently under appeal and a final legal precedent has not been set. The minister emphasizes that she believes ministers should not direct police operations, amidst calls from some MPs for government intervention.
items.why_matters: This decision impacts the legal status and future of online alcohol sales in Iceland, affecting businesses and consumer access.

items.title: Brottfallið tengist vanda verknáms
items.summary: A leading researcher on student dropout rates in Iceland suggests that the high number of students leaving secondary education, which has been stable since 2020, may be due to challenges faced by vocational schools. Many students switch from academic studies to vocational training but are turned away because trade schools lack funding and cannot accommodate the increased demand.
items.why_matters: The shortage of vocational training opportunities impacts the supply of skilled labor crucial for the construction and design industries.

items.title: Manstu þegar engum datt í hug að taka til?
items.summary: Mbl's Smartland section is celebrating its 15th anniversary by revisiting past notable stories. One such story from 2013 featured a 382 sqm stone house on Holtsgata in Reykjavík that was listed for 107 million ISK. The property gained attention for being advertised for sale in a remarkably messy and unkempt state.

items.title: 43 innbrots- og þjófnaðarmál á 14 dögum
items.summary: Reykjavík police are investigating 43 burglary and theft cases that occurred in the past two weeks, with 20 of them in the city center. Authorities believe a small group of repeat offenders is responsible for these crimes, often targeting valuables for drug consumption. Police advise residents and businesses to secure their properties.
items.why_matters: The increase in burglaries and thefts affects property owners and local security in Reykjavík.

items.title: Rjómabú í Flóa til sýnis í sumar
items.summary: The historic Baugsstaðir Creamery in Flói is open to visitors this summer, showcasing its original equipment and operation from 1905 to 1952. It stands as a testament to early technological development and local design in Icelandic agriculture. The creamery now functions as a preserved museum, managed by the Árnesinga Folk Museum.

items.title: Myndir: Eiki Hauks og Sigga Beinteins stálu senunni
items.summary: The Kótelettan music festival took place in Selfoss, featuring performances by various Icelandic artists like Eiríkur Hauksson and Sigga Beinteins. The event was well-attended and created a positive atmosphere, with a BBQ festival and family activities also planned for the weekend.

items.title: Neyða íslensk yfirvöld til að heyra sögur fórnarlamba spillingar
items.summary: Transparency International has assisted over 1,000 Namibians in filing compensation claims against the Icelandic fishing company Samherji and its employees. These claims, related to alleged bribery in Namibia, have been submitted to the Icelandic District Prosecutor, hoping to be included in a potential criminal case. The investigation into Samherji has been ongoing since 2019, but no charges have been filed yet.
items.why_matters: This case could set a precedent for how Icelandic authorities handle international corporate corruption and victim compensation.
items.spin_note: The headline suggests Icelandic authorities are being forced to act, but the article clarifies that the claims have only been submitted and their acceptance is uncertain.

items.title: Telur Instagram og Facebook stuðla að netfíkn
items.summary: The European Commission's preliminary investigation suggests Meta's Facebook and Instagram designs contribute to internet addiction, especially among youth, by using tailored content, autoplay, and endless scrolling. The Digital Services Act (DSA), under which the investigation was conducted, is being implemented in Iceland. Meta could face fines up to 6% of its global turnover if the findings are upheld.
items.why_matters: The Digital Services Act, being implemented in Iceland, will regulate how major online platforms operate, potentially impacting user experience and platform design.

items.title: Eldur í þaki fjögurra hæða blokkar í Bryggjuhverfi
items.summary: A fire broke out in the roof of a four-story apartment building in Bryggjuhverfi, Reykjavík, while workers were melting roofing felt. All available firefighters responded, and residents safely evacuated, with no injuries reported. The roof was completely destroyed.
items.why_matters: This major accident caused significant damage to a residential building in Reykjavík.

items.title: Áframhaldandi vandamál með Neyðarlínusímtöl – Ástralir viðurkenna mistök
items.summary: A woman in Reykjavík was unable to reach the emergency line to report a fire, highlighting ongoing issues with emergency calls in Iceland following the shutdown of 2G and 3G networks. Iceland was the second country after Australia to implement this change, where similar problems have been linked to multiple deaths. Other European nations have delayed their 2G/3G shutdowns after learning from Australia's experience.
items.why_matters: The failure of emergency call services due to the 2G/3G shutdown poses a direct threat to public safety and could lead to preventable deaths in Iceland.

items.title: Viðgerð í Búrfellsvirkjun á lokametrunum – orkuskerðingum aflétt
items.summary: A transformer at the Búrfell power station experienced a breakdown, leading to temporary power curtailments for some industrial users in Iceland. The repair is now nearing completion, and the power system has returned to normal operation, with all curtailments lifted.
items.why_matters: It ensures the continued reliable operation of critical energy infrastructure for Icelandic industries.

items.title: Atvinnuvegaráðherra um Elkem: „Lykilmarkmiðið okkar allra að verja alþjóðlega samkeppnishæfni“
items.summary: Elkem Iceland's parent company has classified its Icelandic operations as discontinued and is preparing assets for sale, citing negative impacts from EU tariffs. The Icelandic Minister of Industries, Hanna Katrín Friðriksson, states that the government is monitoring the situation and is concerned about Iceland's international competitiveness amidst global trade wars. She emphasizes the government's ongoing efforts to advocate for Icelandic interests and ensure the competitiveness of domestic companies.
items.why_matters: This situation highlights the vulnerability of Icelandic industries to international trade policies and could impact jobs and economic output.

items.title: Markmið Íslands ýfa fjaðrir í Evrópu
items.summary: Individual European parliament members are expressing opposition to Iceland's demand for a permanent exemption from the EU's common fisheries policy, should it pursue accession. The Icelandic Foreign Minister downplays this, stating that member state leaders are more open to negotiation, while the head of the Icelandic fishing industry acknowledges the demands are significant and could make accession talks difficult.
items.why_matters: The debate over fisheries policy is a major obstacle to Iceland's potential EU accession, which would have profound economic and political consequences.

items.title: „Við höfum áhyggjur en við erum ekki að panikka“
items.summary: The chairman of the Association of Architectural Firms (Samark) reports a decline in projects for architects, particularly in housing development, despite demand. While some firms expect stability, others anticipate a decrease in work, with some layoffs already occurring among contractors. The article highlights concerns about the type, location, and pricing of housing being built, as many apartments remain unsold.
items.why_matters: This article indicates a slowdown in the construction and design sectors, which could impact housing supply and the broader economy.

items.title: „Munum ekki hafa um annað að ræða en að ráðast að lífskjörum alþýðufólks,“ verði evran tekin upp
items.summary: Sólveig Anna Jónsdóttir, head of the Efling union, argues that adopting the euro would force Iceland to cut living standards during future economic crises. She and lawyer Sveinn Andri Sveinsson discussed the "Áfram Ísland" society, which opposes EU accession talks. Sveinn Andri criticized financial and real estate companies for profiting from high inflation and interest rates, citing the real estate company Heimar as an example.
items.why_matters: This article discusses potential major shifts in Iceland's economic policy (euro adoption, EU accession) and their direct impact on inflation, interest rates, and the living standards of the population.

items.title: Telur Sindra og Ísidór geta sótt tugi milljóna
items.summary: The high-profile "terrorism case" in Iceland, involving Sindri Snær Birgisson and Ísidór Natansson, has officially concluded as the state prosecutor will not appeal their acquittal. Their lawyer believes they can now seek tens of millions in compensation from the state for the four years their lives were disrupted by the accusations. The lawyer also criticized the initial police handling of the case.
items.why_matters: The conclusion of this high-profile case and the potential for significant state compensation highlight issues of legal process and state accountability.

items.title: Breytingarnar hafi skort skynsamlegan rökstuðning
items.summary: The Minister of Environment, Energy and Climate has signed a regulatory change that removes the requirement for advertising operating permits and a four-week comment period for businesses and public services. This aims to reduce regulatory burden and delays, which previously impacted the opening of new public buildings like schools and kindergartens. Health committees can now immediately issue or change permits, ahead of a larger systemic change in 2027.
items.why_matters: This regulatory change will streamline the permit process, reducing delays and regulatory burden for businesses and public services, including the opening of new public buildings.

items.title: AliExpress-lögreglufatnaður varðar ekki ráðherra
items.summary: The Minister of Justice will not intervene in the South Iceland police's purchase of jackets from AliExpress. The ministry stated that individual police departments are independent in their procurement decisions, despite questions about whether the purchase bypassed the National Commissioner of the Police and violated regulations on police uniforms.

items.title: Mætti Kristrún eiga byssuna?
items.summary: The article discusses whether Icelandic Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir can keep a pistol gifted by the Turkish President to NATO leaders. Ministerial ethics rules advise caution with valuable gifts, and the gun's engraving with Kristrún's name complicates whether it's a personal or official gift.
items.why_matters: This story highlights the ethical considerations and transparency expected of high-ranking government officials regarding gifts received in their official capacity.

items.title: KEA hótel láta flýta dagskrá rokkhátíðar
items.summary: Organizers of the "Rokk í Reykjavík" festival at Dillon bar were forced to move their schedule an hour earlier, now ending at 8 PM, due to noise complaints from the nearby Sand Hotel, owned by KEA Hotels. The bar owner, Jón Bjarni Steinsson, received an email from the hotel manager citing permit issues and informing authorities. He expressed frustration, noting other hotels are more accommodating.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights ongoing tensions between nightlife venues and hotels in downtown Reykjavík, potentially impacting future cultural events.

items.title: Kona slasaðist á Falljökli
items.summary: A woman was injured on Falljökull glacier, prompting a Coast Guard helicopter rescue. Although her injuries were not severe, the challenging terrain made a ground evacuation difficult. She was transported to Skaftafell for medical attention.

items.title: Viðar og Sveinn selja sögufrægt einbýli í 101
items.summary: Chef Sveinn Kjartansson and director Viðar Eggertsson are selling their historic 1901 detached house in downtown Reykjavík for 139.9 million ISK. The couple renovated the 130 sqm, three-story property, including a kitchen redesign with the help of an interior architect, while respecting its original character.

items.title: Fjölga greiðsluleiðum til að mæta nýjum ógnum
items.summary: The Central Bank of Iceland is implementing new payment solutions to enhance the resilience of the country's financial system against cyberattacks and technical failures. Initiatives include enabling offline card payments for essential goods and developing an independent domestic payment system for in-store bank transfers, reducing reliance on foreign card companies. These changes aim to ensure the economy can function even during disruptions.
items.why_matters: This initiative ensures that Iceland's economy can continue to function and people can purchase essential goods even if internet or foreign payment systems fail.

items.title: Þrýsti á Trump að stöðva átökin í Íran
items.summary: Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir states that Icelandic inflation, currently at 5.2%, is being driven up by the Iran conflict and associated oil price increases, threatening to trigger wage agreement clauses. She discussed the conflict's impact with Donald Trump and urged Icelandic businesses to help curb price increases to prevent further inflation.
items.why_matters: High inflation and the potential activation of wage agreement clauses directly affect the cost of living and economic stability in Iceland.
items.spin_note: The headline emphasizes the PM's international diplomacy, while the article's core focus for the owner is the domestic economic impact of the Iran conflict on Icelandic inflation and wage agreements.

items.title: Hryðjuverkamálinu lokið — Ríkissaksóknari áfrýjar ekki
items.summary: The State Prosecutor has decided not to appeal the Landsréttur (Court of Appeals) judgment in the so-called terrorism case. The two defendants were convicted of firearms violations, receiving 18 and 15-month sentences, but were acquitted of the more serious terrorism charges. This decision concludes a case that began in 2022, where the men were suspected of planning mass killings and had discussed these plans while possessing numerous firearms.
items.why_matters: This concludes a high-profile case involving serious allegations of domestic terrorism and firearms violations, setting a legal precedent for how such cases are handled in Iceland.

items.title: Neitar að hafa stungið mann í bílakjallara og segist hafa haldið á afrískum tannbursta
items.summary: A man's pre-trial detention has been confirmed by the Court of Appeal in a case where he is accused of attempted murder in a parking garage. The victim suffered life-threatening injuries from being hit by a car, beaten, and stabbed. The accused denies the stabbing, claiming he was holding an "African toothbrush" despite video evidence.

items.title: „Þeirra ævi fór bara á pásu allan þennan tíma“
items.summary: The "so-called terrorism case" in Iceland has concluded, with the prosecutor deciding not to appeal the Court of Appeals' verdict to the Supreme Court. The two defendants were convicted of weapons law violations and sentenced to 18 and 15 months in prison. Their lawyer announced that they will seek significant compensation from the state due to the lengthy legal process and the impact on their lives.
items.why_matters: This concludes a high-profile legal case in Iceland and may result in substantial compensation claims against the state.

items.title: Afgreiðslu starfsleyfa flýtt um allt að fjórar vikur
items.summary: Icelandic authorities have expedited the processing of operating permits for various businesses by removing the requirement for a four-week public comment period. This regulatory change, stemming from recent legislation, aims to reduce delays and create a more flexible environment for new and expanding businesses. The affected sectors include guesthouses, breweries, schools, and healthcare facilities.
items.why_matters: This policy change aims to reduce red tape and accelerate business operations across various sectors in Iceland.

items.title: „Það er erfitt að sjá þetta“
items.summary: A fire broke out in the roof of an apartment building in Naustabryggja 20, reportedly caused by a spark during roof repair work. Residents were evacuated, and at least one top-floor apartment sustained significant water damage.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights the risks associated with building maintenance and can lead to significant disruption and damage for affected residents.

items.title: Innflutningur á glæpaklíkum og spurningin um ESB
items.summary: The article promotes an episode of the talk show "Spursmál" which discusses two main topics. The first is a major drug smuggling operation linked to an Albanian man granted Icelandic citizenship in 2015, sparking debate about past immigration decisions. The second topic is a discussion with Dr. Björn Zoëga, who argues against Iceland joining the EU in an upcoming referendum.
items.why_matters: The drug smuggling case raises questions about immigration policy and national security, and the EU discussion concerns a major national policy decision.

items.title: Ný brú yfir Breiðholtsbraut tekin í notkun
items.summary: A new bridge over Breiðholtsbraut and new traffic lights at the Arnarnesvegur intersection have been opened. The Icelandic Road and Coastal Administration reports a smooth opening, with most drivers quickly adapting to the new layout. This infrastructure improvement aims to alleviate previous traffic queues at the now-closed intersection.
items.why_matters: This new infrastructure aims to improve traffic flow and reduce congestion in the capital region.

items.title: Ellefu mánuðir frá goslokum
items.summary: Nearly a year after the last eruption in the Sundhnúkagígaröð, experts anticipate another eruption due to continued magma accumulation and land uplift. While no immediate eruption is indicated, it could occur with little warning, and a larger eruption is possible. Defense barriers are reportedly ready.
items.why_matters: This matters because ongoing volcanic activity poses a risk to infrastructure and communities in the affected region.

items.title: Telja eldinn slokknaðan: Talsvert tjón á einni íbúð
items.summary: A fire at Naustabryggja 20 in Reykjavík's Bryggjuhverfið has been extinguished, but caused considerable water and fire damage to one apartment. Firefighters are now ensuring no embers remain and are cleaning up water from the operations.

items.title: Stofna rannsóknarsetur um íslenska hestinn
items.summary: A new research center for the Icelandic horse will be established at Hólar in Hjaltadalur, a historic center for horse knowledge. This initiative, supported by the University of Iceland and the Ministry of Culture, aims to conduct in-depth studies on the Icelandic horse. The horse is considered vital to the nation's identity, economy, and culture.
items.why_matters: The establishment of this center aims to preserve and develop knowledge about a key part of Icelandic heritage and identity.

items.title: Metár en benda á óvissu um framtíðina
items.summary: Faxaflóahafnir's annual report highlights the need to decide on the future of Reykjavík harbor, considering the planned Sundabraut project and the trend of port redevelopments in other cities. The report also mentions proposals for changes to Reykjavík's master plan to facilitate Sundabraut and address its impact on port operations. While the port had a record financial year, the focus is on future urban planning.
items.why_matters: This discussion will shape the future development and infrastructure of Reykjavík's harbor area and surrounding city.

items.title: Rannsókn á upptökum brunans lokið: Meta tjónið
items.summary: Police have concluded their initial investigation into a fire at an apartment building in Naustabryggja 20, with insurance companies now assessing the damage. The fire department spent hours removing water from a top-floor apartment, and the fire is suspected to have started during roof work involving melting roofing felt.
items.why_matters: This fire caused significant damage to an apartment building, impacting residents and potentially raising questions about construction safety practices.

items.title: Sagðist hafa borið afrískan tannbursta en ekki hníf
items.summary: The Icelandic Court of Appeals has upheld the continued detention of one of three men accused of attempted murder in the Höfðatorg case. The man is accused of attacking a person in a parking garage, hitting them with an object, and stabbing them. He claimed he was holding an "African toothbrush" when security footage showed him with a weapon.
items.why_matters: This case highlights ongoing serious crime and the judicial process in Iceland.

items.title: Innflutningur háður leyfi lögreglu
items.summary: The article clarifies that importing firearms into Iceland requires a police permit, a point confirmed by customs officials. This inquiry arose after Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir received a pistol as a gift from the Turkish President. Customs noted that questions about diplomatic exemptions or weapon deactivation fall outside their jurisdiction.
items.why_matters: It clarifies the application of weapons import laws and customs procedures, even for high-ranking officials.

items.title: Myndir: Kótelettan sett í 16. sinn
items.summary: The Kótelettan music, family, and barbecue festival has commenced in Selfoss for its 16th year. The event includes two nights of concerts featuring various Icelandic artists and a family day, with thousands of attendees expected.

items.title: „Hjá mér var dansað á borðum“
items.summary: Investor Ásgeir Bolli Kristinsson is selling his luxurious 682 sqm house in Reykjavík, originally designed by Gísli Halldórsson and Bjarni Marteinsson for conductor Vladimir Ashkenazy. Known as the 'Ashkenazy House,' it features a concert hall, billiard room, and sauna, and is described as a perfect party house. Bolli is selling as he now primarily lives in Spain.

items.title: Eldur í þaki fjögurra hæða blokkar í Bryggjuhverfi
items.summary: A fire broke out in the roof of a four-story apartment building in Bryggjuhverfi, Reykjavík, while workers were burning roofing felt. Firefighters responded with multiple units, and residents were evacuated, with no injuries reported. The fire spread throughout the roof, causing extensive damage and rendering it completely unusable.
items.why_matters: This incident represents a significant domestic accident, causing extensive damage to a residential building and impacting its residents.

items.title: Milljarða framkvæmdum í Jarðböðunum lokið
items.summary: The Myvatn Nature Baths have reopened after extensive, multi-billion krona renovations. A new reception and service building, expanded facilities, and a new experience area have been added. The design focused on creating a modern facility that blends with the surrounding natural environment.
items.why_matters: This multi-billion krona project enhances a key Icelandic tourist destination and showcases local architectural design principles.

items.title: 17.08.2026 Landsnet býður út fyrstu framkvæmdir vegna Ísallína 3 og 4
items.summary: Landsnet has issued a tender for the first phase of construction for two new high-voltage power lines, Ísallínur 3 and 4, in Hafnarfjörður. This project involves extensive earthworks and foundations for new masts. It aims to strengthen electricity transmission to the Straumsvík aluminum smelter and is part of the ongoing development of the power transmission system in the capital region.
items.why_matters: This project will strengthen the electricity grid in the capital region, ensuring reliable power supply to a major industrial area.

items.title: Skoða framtíð Elkem á Íslandi
items.summary: Elkem's Icelandic operations are struggling, leading its Norwegian parent company to review the business's future and explore investment options. Despite the financial difficulties and an accounting classification as a "discontinued operation," the Icelandic CEO insists there are no plans to sell and the goal is to protect and potentially increase jobs at the Grundartangi plant.
items.why_matters: The future of Elkem's operations could significantly impact jobs and the industrial sector in Iceland.

items.title: Kröfu um auglýsingu og umsagnarfrest starfsleyfa aflétt
items.summary: The government has lifted the requirement for public advertising and a four-week comment period for operating licenses issued by health committees for many types of businesses, including accommodations and schools. This temporary change, enacted via new regulations following a recent law, aims to streamline processes before municipal health committees are abolished and their functions transferred to the Environment and Energy Agency at year-end.
items.why_matters: This policy change simplifies the process for businesses to obtain or amend operating licenses, potentially speeding up development and reducing administrative burdens.

items.title: Skipti um skoðun eftir fjórðu höfnunina
items.summary: Icelandic playwright Hafsteinn Níelsson, initially rejected multiple times from acting school, found his calling in playwriting. His musical, "Ormstunga," co-written with Ólíver Þorsteinsson, has become a hit at the National Theatre. Níelsson reflects on how his initial setbacks ultimately led to his success in the arts.

items.title: Breytingin hefur styrkt stöðuna
items.summary: Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir announced that changes in NATO's defense spending metrics have significantly improved Iceland's reported contribution, now nearing 1% of GDP. This increase is attributed to the inclusion of previously unreported defense-related infrastructure investments and support for Ukraine. The PM noted that these changes better reflect Iceland's actual contributions.
items.why_matters: This policy change clarifies Iceland's financial contributions to NATO and its defense infrastructure spending.

items.title: Engin fordæmi um undanþágur
items.summary: A Danish minister has stated that no current EU member state has permanent exemptions from the EU's common fisheries policy, raising questions about Iceland's potential EU accession. This implies that if Iceland were to join, EU law would likely supersede national control over marine resources. An Irish MEP also voiced opposition to any special exemptions for Iceland.
items.why_matters: This discussion is crucial for Iceland as potential EU membership could significantly alter its control over its vital fishing resources and national sovereignty.

items.title: Ölvaður undir stýri að horfa á HM í símanum
items.summary: Police in the capital region reported several incidents from their overnight log. These include a driver arrested for being drunk, driving without a license, and watching a World Cup game on his phone. Other incidents under investigation are a break-in in the city center and property damage at a hotel.
items.why_matters: This article highlights ongoing issues with public safety and law enforcement in the capital region.

items.title: Fyrir hverja er kerfið?
items.summary: A neurosurgeon criticizes the Icelandic healthcare system for long waiting lists, arguing that current funding and contracts with Icelandic Health Insurance are insufficient to meet patient needs. He highlights the economic costs to society from delayed treatment and warns that limiting doctors' ability to work could lead to a brain drain.
items.why_matters: Long waiting lists in healthcare lead to increased suffering for patients, higher overall costs for society, and a potential loss of skilled medical professionals.

items.title: Myndband: Sigldu fyrir látinn skipstjóra
items.summary: Four ships sailed in Fáskrúðsfjörður to honor Bergur Einarsson, a respected ship captain who died at 55 in a motorcycle accident. The ships, from companies he worked for, performed a tribute during his funeral procession. This act of respect highlighted his impact on the local fishing community.

items.title: Býður ullarteppi og hlutabréf upp í skuld
items.summary: Ístex, an Icelandic wool company, is unable to pay farmers cash for their wool due to severe cash flow problems and declining sales of lopi and wool products. Instead, farmers are offered the option to convert their debt into company shares or accept wool blankets as payment. The company attributes its struggles to reduced sales, especially to North America and tourists, but notes some improvements due to cost-cutting and increased exports.
items.why_matters: This situation impacts Icelandic farmers and the domestic wool industry, highlighting economic challenges faced by local businesses.

items.title: Sveitarfélögin fá bílhræin til úrvinnslu
items.summary: The article discusses the persistent problem of abandoned and unlicensed vehicles causing urban blight in the capital area, particularly in Kópavogur. It details the challenges faced by the Health Inspectorate in enforcing their removal and highlights upcoming changes in municipal authority that will require local governments to establish new bylaws to manage these nuisances effectively.
items.why_matters: Upcoming changes in municipal authority mean local governments must create new regulations to effectively manage urban blight from abandoned vehicles, impacting the cleanliness and appearance of the capital region.

items.title: Milljarða framkvæmdum í Jarðböðunum lokið
items.summary: The Mývatn Nature Baths have reopened after extensive, multi-billion krona renovations. The project included a new reception and service building, expanded facilities, and a new experience area, designed to blend with the surrounding natural lava formations.

items.title: Áslaug og Runólfur selja einbýli í leynigötu
items.summary: The article details the sale of a unique 1923 detached house at Haðarstíg 15 in downtown Reykjavík, listed for 145 million ISK. Owned by Áslaug Guðrúnardóttir, the 145 sqm property has undergone extensive renovations, showcasing new interiors and artful decoration. Haðarstígur is described as a charming pedestrian street known for its beautifully preserved houses.

items.title: Bráðavakt allan sólarhringinn á framkvæmdasvæðinu í Vaðölduveri
items.summary: Iceland's first wind farm, Vaðölduver, is under construction with over 200 workers on site. A 24/7 emergency medical service is provided, which also assists the local community. Four of 28 turbines are already built, with the first expected to be operational by late August and all by the end of 2027.
items.why_matters: This project represents a significant development in Iceland's energy infrastructure and renewable energy production.

items.title: Áhugi á að breyta Hópinu í Grindavík í sýningarsal
items.summary: Grindavík town council is considering a proposal to lease the Hópið sports hall for an exhibition space. While welcoming the interest, the council has set four strict conditions, including detailed geological surveys due to fissures under the building, cost analysis for repairs, legal and insurance clarity, and ensuring financial benefits for the town. A final decision, heavily reliant on safety and geological factors, is expected by January 2027.
items.why_matters: This decision will determine the future use of a significant public building in Grindavík, impacting the town's recovery and potential economic activity.

items.title: Hornsteinn hagnast um 1,9 milljarða
items.summary: Hornsteinn, the holding company for major Icelandic construction material suppliers BM Vallá and Björgun-Sement, reported a profit of 1.9 billion ISK in 2025, significantly up from the previous year, largely due to asset sales. The company is also actively engaged in discussions with Reykjavík City regarding the relocation of BM Vallá's operations, with a decision on a new site expected later this year.
items.why_matters: The relocation of a major construction materials supplier like BM Vallá could impact future urban development and construction projects in the capital region.

items.title: Jarðböðin á Mývatni opnuð eftir tímafrekar framkvæmdir
items.summary: The Mývatn Nature Baths have reopened after multi-year, multi-billion króna renovations, featuring a new facility three times larger than the old one, now accommodating up to 600 guests. The project emphasized sustainability and was delayed by the discovery of a large cave, which is now in a protection process.
items.why_matters: This project significantly expands a major tourist attraction and employer, impacting local tourism and infrastructure.

items.title: 13.08.2026 Nýr Landspítali býður út varaaflvélakerfi fyrir Hringbrautarsjúkrahúsið
items.summary: The New National Hospital is tendering for a crucial backup power system for the new Hringbraut hospital. This system will ensure uninterrupted electricity for life-sustaining medical equipment, operating rooms, and intensive care units, preventing disruptions during power outages.
items.why_matters: This system is vital for the safe and continuous operation of the new National Hospital, ensuring essential medical services are not disrupted by power failures.

items.title: First Water semur um 4.300 tonn af steypueiningum fyrir landeldi í Þorlákshöfn
items.summary: First Water has contracted Norwegian company Overhalla Betongbygg for 4,300 tons of precast concrete units for a new land-based salmon farm in Þorlákshöfn. This 55 million NOK agreement involves building eight large fish farming tanks, each 28 meters in diameter, to be delivered by early 2027. This first phase will double First Water's annual production capacity from 5,000 to 10,000 tons of salmon, with long-term plans to reach 60,000 tons.
items.why_matters: This project represents a significant investment and expansion in Iceland's aquaculture industry, impacting the local economy and infrastructure in Þorlákshöfn.

items.title: Fannar leiðir hagræðingarteymi í Reykjanesbæ
items.summary: Reykjanesbær's town council has established a temporary team to improve administrative efficiency and financial operations. Led by former Grindavík mayor Fannar Jónasson, the team will review existing operations and implement changes to ensure better use of residents' tax money and improved services.
items.why_matters: This initiative aims to improve how the municipality uses tax funds and delivers services to its residents.

items.title: Þjóðverjar rekja um 5.000 dauðsföll til hitabylgju
items.summary: German authorities estimate over 5,000 deaths in the country are linked to a recent heatwave, primarily in June. Most victims were over 75, with a significant spike in deaths in cities like Cologne. The heatwave made June the warmest in Western Europe on record.
items.why_matters: This event highlights the severe and deadly impact of climate change and extreme weather events on public health, even in developed nations.

items.title: Búið að hreinsa málningu af tröppunum við Grafarvogskirkju
items.summary: The steps of Grafarvogskirkja have been cleaned after the Icelandic flag was painted over the rainbow flag. Police are investigating the vandalism as a potential hate crime. The church plans to repaint the rainbow flag in the coming days.
items.why_matters: This incident is being investigated as a potential hate crime, highlighting social tensions and legal responses to vandalism.

items.title: Ný brú yfir Breiðholtsbraut opnuð í fyrramálið
items.summary: A new bridge over Breiðholtsbraut, connecting Jaðarsel in Reykjavík and Vatnsendahvarf in Kópavogur, is scheduled to open tomorrow morning. This opening is a major milestone in the construction of the new Arnarnesvegur, which also includes new traffic lights and road sections. Drivers should be aware of temporary road closures tonight and new traffic arrangements.
items.why_matters: This new infrastructure project will significantly alter traffic flow and connectivity in the capital region, impacting daily commutes and urban development.

items.title: Bíddu ha? „Metnaðarfull fyrsta plata“
items.summary: The article reviews "Bíddu ha?", the debut album by Icelandic band BKPM, which recently celebrated its one-year anniversary and was named "album of the week" on Rás 2. The review describes the album's diverse tracks, musical style, and lyrical themes, praising its ambition and production quality.

items.title: Njósnaskipið enn innan efnahagslögsögunnar
items.summary: A Russian spy ship, the Yuri Ivanov, has been observed within Iceland's economic zone north of the country since the beginning of the week. The Icelandic Coast Guard is monitoring its movements, noting the situation is similar to a previous sighting in June.
items.why_matters: The presence of a foreign spy ship in Iceland's economic zone raises national security and sovereignty concerns.

items.title: Þúsund Namibíumenn krefjast skaðabóta vegna Samherjamálsins
items.summary: Over a thousand Namibians have filed compensation claims in Iceland against Samherji, alleging they suffered job losses and hardship due to the company's alleged bribery and corruption in Namibia. Transparency International is supporting these claims, which seek to be included in any potential criminal case against Samherji in Iceland. The claimants lost their livelihoods when fishing quotas were allegedly diverted to Samherji or when Samherji abruptly left Namibia.
items.why_matters: This case could set a precedent for foreign victims of alleged corruption by Icelandic companies to seek justice and compensation within Iceland's legal system.

items.title: Dómari neitar frávísun og hoppukastalamálið á leið í aðalmeðferð
items.summary: A district judge in North Iceland East has rejected a request to dismiss the 'bouncy castle case,' meaning the trial will proceed. Five men are accused of negligent bodily harm after a bouncy castle in Akureyri became unsecured, injuring four children in 2021. The case is now expected to go to a main hearing this autumn.
items.why_matters: The ruling means the legal process for a serious accident involving children will continue, potentially setting a precedent for public safety negligence.

items.title: Harðnandi átök auka líkur á forsendubresti kjarasamninga
items.summary: The Minister of Finance is increasingly pessimistic about the stability of current wage agreements, citing escalating global conflicts that are driving up oil prices and, consequently, inflation. The article warns that if annual inflation surpasses 4.7% by the end of August, existing wage agreements could be terminated. The minister also dismissed criticism from the business sector regarding the Competition Authority's review of fuel price reductions.
items.why_matters: The potential breakdown of wage agreements due to rising inflation and oil prices could significantly affect household incomes and the overall economy.

items.title: Geimfarar NASA skoða almyrkvann frá Snæfellsnesi
items.summary: Thirty NASA astronauts and scientists will visit Snæfellsnes, Iceland, in August to research a total solar eclipse. They will bring specialized equipment and collaborate with the Snæfellsnes National Park. The research aims to collect samples during the two-minute eclipse.

items.title: 71,3 % íbúa Flóahrepps vilja ekki sameiningu
items.summary: A survey in Flóahrepp municipality revealed that 71.3% of residents oppose merging with another municipality, while 28.7% were in favor. The mayor stated that the clear results indicate residents are satisfied with their independent municipality, which is growing and stable. Consequently, the municipal council is not expected to pursue merger discussions further at this time.
items.why_matters: This decision means Flóahrepp will remain an independent municipality, impacting its future administrative structure and local development planning.

items.title: Bráðavakt allan sólarhringinn á framkvæmdasvæðinu í Vaðölduveri
items.summary: Construction is underway for Iceland's first wind farm, Vaðölduver, with over 200 workers on site. Four of 28 turbines are already erected, with the first expected to be operational by late August. A 24-hour emergency medical service is provided on-site, also assisting the local community.
items.why_matters: This project marks a significant step in Iceland's renewable energy infrastructure with the country's first wind farm.

items.title: Talar gegn undanþágum fyrir Ísland
items.summary: An Irish MEP has voiced strong opposition to the European Union granting Iceland special exemptions from its common fisheries policy should Iceland pursue EU membership. He emphasized that rules must apply equally to all member states, citing past sacrifices made by Irish fishermen.
items.why_matters: This stance highlights a significant potential obstacle for Iceland in any future EU accession negotiations, as fisheries policy is a critical national interest.

items.title: Verðlaunahugmyndin sem átti að fara í ruslið
items.summary: An Icelandic advertising agency, Pipar\TBWA, won two bronze awards at the prestigious Cannes Lions festival for their "¡Hola!" campaign for the asphalt company Colas. The campaign, which started as a joke idea, aimed to raise awareness and pressure for better road maintenance in Iceland. This marks the first time an Icelandic agency has won two "all-Icelandic" lions for a single campaign.

items.title: Lögregla þekkti þjófana á upptöku
items.summary: The article reports on several incidents from the capital region police log, including a break-in at a restaurant where police identified and arrested the perpetrators. It also details two other residential break-ins currently under investigation and a public disturbance involving an intoxicated individual.

items.title: Samskipti Þorgerðar og Jettens ekki í yfirlitinu
items.summary: MP Diljá Mist Einarsdóttir criticizes Foreign Minister Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir for repeatedly attacking Morgunblaðið. The dispute stems from the newspaper's coverage of a Dutch parliamentary debate where the Dutch Prime Minister confirmed that EU accession requires adopting the common fisheries policy. Diljá also alleges that the Foreign Minister's official communication records do not show any contact with the Dutch PM, despite the Minister's claims.
items.why_matters: This article highlights political tensions and transparency issues surrounding Iceland's potential EU accession and its implications for key sectors like fisheries.

items.title: Telur varanlegar undanþágur útilokaðar
items.summary: Vilhjálmur Birgisson, chairman of the Akranes Workers' Union, commented on statements by the Dutch Prime Minister, indicating that permanent exemptions from the EU's common fisheries policy are unlikely for new member states. Birgisson emphasized that Iceland should maintain full control over its valuable natural resources.
items.why_matters: This discussion highlights a critical hurdle for any potential Icelandic EU accession, directly impacting the nation's sovereignty over its vital fishing resources and economy.

items.title: Borgarbúar hvattir til að halda sig heima
items.summary: Authorities in West Iceland are making extensive preparations for the upcoming total solar eclipse, which is expected to draw tens of thousands of visitors. They are implementing temporary traffic arrangements, including one-way roads and bus services to viewing spots, and urging capital region residents to watch from home due to anticipated congestion and fully booked accommodations.
items.why_matters: The extensive planning and temporary infrastructure changes will significantly impact travel and accommodation in West Iceland for the eclipse.

items.title: Portúgalskar kvikmyndir í brennidepli á RIFF
items.summary: The Reykjavík International Film Festival (RIFF) will focus on Portuguese cinema this year, showcasing five new films exploring various aspects of Portuguese culture and history. Renowned Portuguese actress María de Medeiros, known for "Pulp Fiction," will visit Iceland to receive an honorary award at the festival.

items.title: Tilraunum til netbrota fjölgar en brotum ekki
items.summary: Police in the capital region are receiving a significantly higher number of reports about attempted cybercrimes, indicating increased public awareness, while the number of successful crimes has not risen proportionally. However, the financial damage from successful cybercrimes has substantially increased this year, reaching 427 million ISK so far. The article details various types of online fraud, noting that investment and romance scams cause the most financial harm.
items.why_matters: This article highlights a growing threat of financial cybercrime to individuals and businesses in Iceland, with hundreds of millions of krónur lost, despite increased public awareness.
items.spin_note: The headline suggests successful crimes are not increasing, but the article reveals that the financial damage from these crimes has significantly increased.

items.title: Jarðböðin á Mývatni opnuð eftir tímafrekar framkvæmdir
items.summary: The Mývatn Nature Baths have reopened after several years of extensive construction, with the new facility being three times larger and the lagoon expanded by 35%. The multi-billion króna project emphasized sustainability, using local materials, and faced delays due to the discovery of a large cave now undergoing protection.
items.why_matters: The reopening of this major tourist attraction and employer impacts the regional economy and showcases sustainable Icelandic design.

items.title: Primex ræsir vélarnar á ný eftir stórbruna í fyrra
items.summary: The Primex factory in Siglufjörður has restarted shrimp shell processing after an 8-month halt caused by a major fire last October. The fire resulted in 1.3 billion ISK in damages, representing a significant portion of all fire insurance claims in Iceland last year. All 20 employees retained their jobs during the shutdown.
items.why_matters: The restart of this factory is important for the local economy of Siglufjörður and its 20 employees.

items.title: Undirrituðu samning um samruna: Daði Már viðstaddur
items.summary: The boards of two Icelandic pension funds, SL lífeyrissjóður and Almenna – Lífsverks lífeyrissjóður, have signed a merger agreement. If approved, the combined entity would become the fourth largest pension fund in Iceland, aiming to strengthen pension rights, improve service, and achieve operational efficiencies for its members. The Finance Minister was present and committed to facilitating necessary legal changes.
items.why_matters: This merger could lead to stronger pension rights, better service, and potentially higher returns for members of the involved pension funds.

items.title: Fyrrverandi bæjarstjóri leiðir hagræðingarteymi
items.summary: Reykjanesbær has formed a new team, led by former Grindavík mayor Fannar Jónasson, to enhance administrative efficiency and financial operations. The initiative aims to ensure taxpayer money is utilized effectively and to improve the municipality's overall financial stability.
items.why_matters: This initiative aims to improve the financial management and efficiency of Reykjanesbær, potentially affecting local services and the use of taxpayer money.

items.title: Meðallaunþeginn fer á mis við 15 milljónir
items.summary: A new study reveals that Icelandic private pension funds have significantly lower returns than general pension funds, causing average wage earners to miss out on an estimated 15 million ISK in savings by retirement. The Consumers' Association chairman attributes this disparity to banks holding a large portion of private pension savings in low-yield indexed bank accounts, raising concerns about banks using these funds for cheap financing.
items.why_matters: This issue could significantly reduce the retirement savings of average Icelanders, impacting their financial security in old age.

items.title: „Sorglegt“ að fólk vilji fela fánanum ógeðfellt hlutverk
items.summary: A government minister has condemned the defacement of a Pride flag at a church in Grafarvogur, which was painted over with Icelandic flag colors. Police are investigating the incident as a hate crime. The minister emphasized that both the Icelandic flag and the Pride flag are symbols of unity and have important places.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights ongoing social tensions regarding LGBTQ+ rights and national symbols in Iceland, leading to a police investigation into a hate crime.

items.title: Sendi mynd af kynfærum karlmanns í fullri reisn
items.summary: An East Iceland district court has sentenced a man to a two-month suspended prison sentence for a sexual offense and indecency. He was found guilty of sending sexually explicit messages and an image of male genitals to a 15-year-old girl via Snapchat. The man was also ordered to pay 400,000 ISK in damages to the victim and nearly 2 million ISK in legal costs.
items.why_matters: This ruling demonstrates the legal consequences for online sexual harassment and indecency involving minors in Iceland.

items.title: Skipti úr já-i í nei
items.summary: Gunnar Ármannsson, a lawyer, has changed his long-held stance from supporting to opposing Iceland's EU accession. He argues that joining the EU would require ceding too much sovereignty, legislative, judicial, and executive power to supranational institutions, which he finds unacceptable. He emphasizes that a referendum on accession talks is a significant commitment, not just an exploratory step.
items.why_matters: This discussion on EU accession directly impacts Iceland's future sovereignty, economic policy, and international relations.

items.title: Mála tröppurnar aftur þegar veður leyfir
items.summary: The rainbow flag painted on the steps of Grafarvogskirkja church was covered with the Icelandic flag by unknown individuals. The incident is being investigated as a hate crime. The church plans to repaint the steps with the rainbow flag when weather allows, inviting community help.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights an ongoing issue of hate crime and intolerance in Iceland, prompting a police investigation.

items.title: „Vitleysan“ hjá borginni bitnar ekki á sölutölum
items.summary: Reykjavík City's new food policy, which aims to remove processed meats from menus at city facilities serving children, has reportedly had little impact on hot dog sales this summer. Despite the policy, hot dogs remain popular in city summer activities, and a major hot dog producer has not seen a decline in sales, with its CEO criticizing the policy as "nonsense."
items.why_matters: This city policy affects food choices for children in municipal programs and reflects a debate on city intervention.

items.title: Margir bíða með að sýna á spilin
items.summary: The article details the preparations by various Icelandic organizations for the upcoming national referendum on EU accession talks, scheduled for August 29th. Both pro- and anti-EU groups are planning events and campaigns across the country to engage the public. Some academic institutions are still considering their involvement in the discussions.
items.why_matters: A national referendum on EU accession talks could significantly alter Iceland's economic and political landscape.

items.title: Neitar að frávísa hoppukastalamálinu
items.summary: A district court judge in North Iceland has rejected a request to dismiss the "bouncy castle case." This means the case, involving five men charged with negligent bodily harm after a serious accident in Akureyri in 2021, will proceed to trial this autumn. Four children were injured in the incident, one severely, due to alleged inadequate securing of the bouncy castle.
items.why_matters: This case addresses accountability for a serious accident that caused lasting harm to children, setting a precedent for safety negligence.

items.title: Tröppurnar litlausar að sinni
items.summary: Unidentified individuals painted an Icelandic flag over a rainbow flag on the stairs leading to Grafarvogskirkja in Reykjavík. The Icelandic flag has since been removed, and the incident is being investigated as a hate crime. The church plans to repaint the rainbow flag when conditions allow.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights ongoing social tensions and the legal response to hate crimes in Iceland.

items.title: Keyrði yfir umferðareyju og hafnaði á skilti
items.summary: A driver lost control of their car in Kópavogur, driving over a traffic island and crashing into a sign. Police and multiple ambulances responded to the scene, and at least one person was transported to the emergency room.

items.title: Rammagerðin fær að leita nauðasamninga
items.summary: Rammagerðin ehf., a company operating three retail stores in Reykjavík, has been granted permission by a district court to seek composition agreements with its creditors. This process allows the company to negotiate debt payments or forgiveness to avoid bankruptcy. Creditors are invited to a meeting to vote on the proposal.
items.why_matters: This indicates financial distress for a notable Icelandic retail chain, reflecting broader economic conditions.

items.title: Ekki eigi að gagnrýna Ólaf Ragnar fyrir andstöðuna
items.summary: Minister of Justice Þorbjörg Sigríður Gunnlaugsdóttir commented on former President Ólafur Ragnar Grímsson's opposition to EU accession talks. She stated that while his stance shouldn't be criticized, it's not particularly newsworthy given his consistent history of opposing various international agreements. The discussion revolves around a proposed referendum on whether Iceland should begin EU accession negotiations.
items.why_matters: A potential referendum on EU accession talks could significantly alter Iceland's economic and political landscape.

items.title: Flikkað upp á Villa Nova á Sauðárkróki
items.summary: Villa Nova, a prominent and beautiful state-owned house in Sauðárkrókur, is undergoing a much-needed renovation. The building was previously neglected and dirty, but its facelift is now revitalizing the old town.

items.title: Íbúðum í byggingu fækkar en byggingaráformum fjölgar á milli mánaða
items.summary: The number of apartments currently under construction in Iceland has decreased month-over-month, indicating more completions than new starts. However, the number of new building plans (permits issued) has increased. So far this year, over 1,400 new apartments have been completed, with a trend towards smaller detached homes outside the capital region and medium-sized multi-family units overall.
items.why_matters: This data indicates trends in housing supply, affecting market availability and prices.

items.title: Sóttu kaldan og hrakinn ferðamann í Sveinsgil
items.summary: A large-scale search and rescue operation was launched in Sveinsgil, north of Torfajökull, after a tourist called the emergency line. Multiple rescue teams and a Coast Guard helicopter were involved in locating the individual. The tourist was found cold and wet but unharmed and was transported to Reykjavík.

items.title: Íranar beina árásum á Barein og Kúveit
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claims to have attacked US military infrastructure in Bahrain and Kuwait, stating these were retaliatory strikes against US actions. This marks the second consecutive night of military exchanges between the US and Iran, with threats of further escalation.
items.why_matters: This article details an escalating military conflict between Iran and the US, which could have significant geopolitical consequences.

items.title: Olíuverð ekki verið hærra síðan um miðjan síðasta mánuð
items.summary: Global oil prices have risen significantly due to renewed conflict between the US and Iran, with Brent crude reaching $78.80 per barrel. This marks the highest price since mid-last month, driven by concerns over supply disruptions from the Middle East.
items.why_matters: Rising global oil prices can lead to increased fuel costs and contribute to inflation in Iceland.

items.title: Bonnie Tyler er látin
items.summary: Welsh singer Bonnie Tyler, famous for hits like "Total Eclipse of the Heart," has died at the age of 75. Her family announced she passed away unexpectedly in a hospital in Portugal, having previously undergone emergency bowel surgery.

items.title: Bláa Lónið eykur hlut sinn í þremur baðlónum
items.summary: Blue Lagoon hf. is increasing its ownership stake in Norðurböð ehf., which operates Jarðböðin á Mývatni, Sjóböðin á Húsavík, and Vök Baths. This strategic move aims to strengthen Blue Lagoon's operations across Iceland and diversify its risk. The company is also preparing for a listing on the Icelandic stock market.
items.why_matters: This expansion and upcoming IPO signal significant activity in Iceland's tourism and financial sectors, potentially impacting investment opportunities and the broader economy.

items.title: „Það er náttúrulega erfitt að hemja sig“
items.summary: The article discusses the widespread use of AI among Icelandic high school students, who are the first generation to have access to these tools throughout their secondary education. Student and teacher associations express concerns about the potential negative impact on students' writing skills and independent thought, citing a Danish study. Educational leaders are calling for the Icelandic government to develop a comprehensive policy on AI in schools.
items.why_matters: The widespread use of AI in education and the lack of clear policy could significantly impact the critical thinking and writing skills of future generations, requiring governmental action.

items.title: „Hækkum í raun bara af illri nauðsyn“
items.summary: A new chicken restaurant, Tjikký, inside a renovated Krónan supermarket, has higher prices than its predecessor. The manager attributes this to significantly increased raw material costs for chicken, stating they are only raising prices out of necessity to cover expenses.
items.why_matters: This article illustrates how rising raw material costs directly translate to higher consumer prices for everyday goods, reflecting the impact of inflation on household budgets.

items.title: Cosplay: búningalist fyrir allan aldur
items.summary: The article explores cosplay as a costume art form and hobby, highlighting its growing community in Iceland. It features an interview with an Icelandic cosplayer who discusses the challenges of sourcing materials locally and the various sub-groups within the Icelandic cosplay scene.

items.title: Býst ekki við því að hótelið rísi
items.summary: Isavia's plans to build a large hotel at Keflavík Airport are facing opposition from local tourism stakeholders and Reykjanesbær officials. Critics argue the project doesn't align with the region's tourism vision and question if Isavia is exceeding its operational scope. The owner of Hótel Keflavíkur believes the hotel will not be built and that Isavia should prioritize other airport services.
items.why_matters: This project could significantly alter the tourism landscape and development priorities around Keflavík Airport and the Reykjanes peninsula.

items.title: Myndir: Aðgerðir gengu vel við Þjórsá
items.summary: A concrete mixer truck that fell off a bridge into the Þjórsá river was successfully recovered. The driver, who suffered hypothermia, is now recovering at home. Repairs to the bridge were completed, and it has reopened to traffic.
items.why_matters: The incident caused a temporary closure of a bridge on a public road, impacting travel, and required significant rescue and recovery efforts.

items.title: Sóttu kaldan og blautan ferðamann
items.summary: A hiker was rescued by a Coast Guard helicopter and multiple rescue teams after getting into trouble in Sveinsgil by Torfajökull. The search lasted five hours, and the man was found unharmed but cold and wet.

items.title: Ætla að skoða ný tækifæri með íbúunum
items.summary: The Mayor of Reykjavík, Hildur Björnsdóttir, announced plans to revise urban development in Grafarvogur, halting previous densification projects and seeking resident input for new, potentially smaller-scale housing, possibly for seniors. She also criticized the existing Keldnalandið development plan, particularly its transport assumptions, and intends to revise it to create a more viable future neighborhood and secure funding for regional transport infrastructure.
items.why_matters: These planning revisions will directly impact future housing development, infrastructure funding, and the character of several neighborhoods in Reykjavík.

items.title: Fiskveiðistefna ESB ófrávíkjanleg
items.summary: A Dutch parliamentary debate confirmed that any country joining the European Union must fully adopt its common fisheries policy, challenging previous suggestions of potential exemptions for Iceland. This firm stance, reinforced by a parliamentary vote, indicates that Iceland would likely not retain full sovereignty over its fisheries if it were to join the EU.
items.why_matters: This clarifies a major hurdle for Iceland's potential EU accession, as relinquishing control over its vital fisheries sector would have significant economic and sovereignty implications.

items.title: Reyndi að hnupla verkfærum iðnaðarmanna
items.summary: Police in the capital area responded to several incidents overnight, including a man attempting to steal tools from craftsmen at a shopping mall. The tools were recovered, but the suspect escaped. Other incidents included an attempted break-in and seven arrests for driving under the influence.

items.title: Kærður til lögreglu fyrir akstur gröfu
items.summary: Finnur Harðarson has been reported to the police by additional landowners for driving a large excavator off-road on their property near the Stóra-Laxá river. He allegedly caused damage to the land and riverbanks, and previously used the excavator to harass fishermen. Landowners are seeking police investigation and penalties for violations of nature conservation laws.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights ongoing disputes over land use and environmental protection, potentially leading to legal consequences for the individual involved.

items.title: Lýsir áhyggjum af aukinni kostnaðarþátttöku
items.summary: The Association of Physiotherapists is concerned about a new "arrival fee" for physiotherapy services, set to begin September 1st, which will directly increase costs for users. They estimate this policy will add over a billion ISK in costs by 2025, significantly impacting pensioners and those with limited financial means. The association criticizes the lack of consultation and warns of reduced access to essential rehabilitation.
items.why_matters: This new fee will directly increase healthcare costs for individuals needing physiotherapy, potentially limiting access to essential services for many.

items.title: Óvissa um leikskólastarf vegna þakleka
items.summary: A kindergarten in Grafarholt, Reynisholt, is experiencing uncertainty in its operations due to a minor roof leak that requires the replacement of the roof's top layer. The city's construction and property services office is preparing for the repair work, which is expected to be completed by October 1st. This situation may affect the kindergarten's ability to accept new children as planned.
items.why_matters: The roof repairs could disrupt kindergarten services, impacting parents and children in the area.

items.title: Framkvæmdir víða í Húnaþingi vestra í sumar
items.summary: The article details various ongoing construction projects in Húnaþing vestra, including extensive renovations of school grounds, sports facilities, and community centers. It also covers significant upgrades to roads, sidewalks, and utility infrastructure like heating pipes, fiber optics, and power cables. The goal is to enhance local services and strengthen the municipality's long-term infrastructure.
items.why_matters: These municipal projects will directly impact local services, infrastructure, and quality of life for residents in Húnaþing vestra.

items.title: Býst ekki við því að hótelið rísi
items.summary: Isavia's plan to build a 200-400 room hotel at Keflavík Airport is facing skepticism. Local hotel owner Steinþór Jónsson and representatives from Reykjanesbær question if the project aligns with the region's tourism vision and if Isavia is exceeding its mandate. Jónsson believes Isavia should prioritize other airport services and that the area already has sufficient hotel capacity.
items.why_matters: This project could significantly impact the tourism landscape and local economy on the Reykjanes peninsula.

items.title: Framkvæmdum við fyrsta áfanga bílaplans við Baug Bjólfs að ljúka
items.summary: The first phase of constructing a parking lot near the Baugur Bjólfs viewpoint in Seyðisfjörður is nearing completion. Work is also underway to clear the walking path to the viewpoint. The project faced delays due to an early winter, and the final stages, including road and path improvements, are planned after the summer tourist season.
items.why_matters: This project improves infrastructure and access to a popular viewpoint in Seyðisfjörður.

items.title: Ný brú yfir Breið­holts­braut opnuð fyrir umferð á föstu­daginn
items.summary: A new bridge over Breiðholtsbraut is opening for traffic on Friday, leading to significant changes in road infrastructure and traffic flow in the capital region. This includes new sections of Arnarnesvegur and Vatnsendavegur, new traffic lights, and the reorganization of a major intersection. These changes are part of the ongoing Arnarnesvegur project.
items.why_matters: This project will alter traffic flow and commuting patterns for residents in the capital region.

items.title: 31.07.2026 MT Ísland leitar að smiðum til framtíðarstarfa
items.summary: MT Ísland ehf., a company specializing in property damage repair and reconstruction, is seeking experienced carpenters for new projects. The company handles water, moisture, mold, and fire damage, offering diverse tasks in a professional team environment.

items.title: Rokkland minnist Megasar
items.summary: RÚV's Rokkland radio show is commemorating the passing of Megas, a highly influential Icelandic musician and lyricist. The program is broadcasting parts of a previously unaired interview from 1997 where Megas discusses his career beginnings and the origin of his stage name.

items.title: Segir hóteláformin gerð í samráði við nærsamfélagið
items.summary: Isavia is moving forward with plans for a new hotel at Keflavík Airport, stating the project is part of a long-term vision and developed in consultation with local communities. However, the mayor of Reykjanesbær has raised concerns about the hotel creating unfair competition for existing businesses and exacerbating parking issues. Isavia clarifies they intend to find a third party to build and operate the hotel, not do it themselves.
items.why_matters: This project could impact local businesses, tourism infrastructure, and parking at Iceland's main international airport.
items.spin_note: The title emphasizes Isavia's claim of consultation, but the article immediately presents the mayor's concerns about the project.

items.title: Spá því að verðbólga verði umfram forsenduákvæði
items.summary: Landsbankinn's analysis department forecasts that inflation will remain at 5.2% in July and is likely to exceed the 4.7% threshold in wage agreements by August. Rising airfares are a primary driver, while lower fuel prices and summer sales offer some downward pressure. Housing costs continue to be the main factor, though their contribution is lessening.
items.why_matters: This forecast suggests inflation could trigger a clause allowing for the termination of wage agreements, impacting many Icelanders.

items.title: Skerða orku til fyrirtækja á Suðurlandi, Vesturlandi og Vestfjörðum um óákveðinn tíma
items.summary: Landsnet is implementing temporary energy cuts to certain businesses in South Iceland, West Iceland, and the Westfjords due to a serious transformer failure at Búrfellsvirkjun and ongoing maintenance. While the cuts are expected to last only a few days and affect a limited number of companies, they highlight vulnerabilities in the national power grid. Repairs are underway, and normal service is anticipated to resume shortly.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights the fragility of Iceland's energy infrastructure and its potential impact on regional businesses.
items.spin_note: The headline's 'indefinitely' sounds more severe than the body's clarification that cuts are expected to last only a few days and affect limited businesses.

items.title: Þrúður Vilhjálmsdóttir er látin
items.summary: Þrúður Vilhjálmsdóttir, a prominent Icelandic actress known for her roles in films like "101 Reykjavík" and "Djúpið," and various TV series, has passed away at 53 after a brief illness. She graduated from the Icelandic Drama School in 1997 and had a prolific career in theater, film, and television.

items.title: Við þurfum bókasöfn rétt eins og við þurfum græn svæði
items.summary: The government's financial plan proposes replacing librarians at the National Library with security guards this autumn, leading to a significant reduction in services. Kamilla Einarsdóttir argues that libraries are essential community spaces, providing peace and quiet, and are crucial given rising loneliness.
items.why_matters: The government's financial plan will reduce services at the National Library, impacting public access to information and community spaces.

items.title: Lögreglan leitar tveggja manna
items.summary: The Capital Region Police are searching for two men in connection with an ongoing investigation. They are asking the public for assistance in locating them.
items.why_matters: The police are seeking public assistance in an ongoing criminal investigation.

items.title: Skemmdarvargar við Grafarvogskirkju náðust á upptöku
items.summary: Police in the capital region have obtained video footage showing two individuals vandalizing the steps of Grafarvogskirkja. The vandals painted over a rainbow flag with the colors of the Icelandic flag. The incident is currently under investigation as a hate crime.

items.title: Áhyggjur og vonbrigði með breytingar á heilbrigðiseftirliti
items.summary: The town council of Vogar expresses concerns and disappointment regarding new legislation that will transfer health and environmental inspection tasks from municipalities to the national Environment and Energy Agency. They highlight worries about potential service disruption, inadequate impact assessment, and the financial burden on municipalities as revenue-generating tasks move to the state while costly ones remain local.
items.why_matters: This policy change could impact the quality and efficiency of health and environmental oversight, and shift financial burdens onto municipalities, potentially affecting local services or taxes.

items.title: Milljarða bótakrafa féll á ágreiningi um það hver sé „hann sjálfur“
items.summary: A court in Iceland rejected Vestmannaeyjar municipality's 2 billion ISK compensation claim against Huginn hf. and VÍS for damage to its water pipeline. The court ruled that maritime law limits liability to 360 million ISK, as the company's board or CEO were not proven to have shown gross negligence, only the crew. The municipality is considering an appeal, as a new pipeline is estimated to cost nearly 3 billion ISK.
items.why_matters: This ruling significantly impacts Vestmannaeyjar municipality's finances and its ability to fund the replacement of critical water infrastructure.

items.title: Bætt brunatjón lækkaði um 23% milli ára
items.summary: Compensated fire damage in Iceland decreased by 23% last year, totaling 3.6 billion ISK. Commercial properties accounted for the majority of costs, largely due to one significant fire, while residential properties saw over 950 million ISK in damages.
items.why_matters: This statistic reflects significant financial losses from property damage across Iceland, which can impact insurance costs and property values.

items.title: Voru í fullum rétti að reka forstjórann
items.summary: A district court in Vestfirðir ruled that the former CEO of the Municipal Collection Agency was rightfully dismissed without notice due to serious misconduct. The CEO had sued the agency for over 90 million ISK for unlawful dismissal, but the court rejected all his claims and ordered him to pay legal costs. This case stems from an investigation into the CEO making an unauthorized contract with a law firm owned by another agency director.
items.why_matters: This ruling highlights accountability for serious misconduct within a public institution and the legal consequences for officials who breach their duties.

items.title: Þýskur læknir myrti að minnsta kosti 15 sjúklinga
items.summary: A German doctor has been sentenced to life in prison for murdering 15 of his palliative care patients by administering lethal sedatives without their consent. He confessed to the crimes, claiming he wanted to spare them suffering. Authorities are investigating 76 additional cases, suggesting he could be one of Germany's most prolific serial killers.

items.title: „Bull og vitleysa“ að nægt rafmagn sé til staðar á Íslandi
items.summary: A factory in Bíldudalur has been forced to halt all production due to power cuts caused by a malfunction in a power plant transformer. The CEO reports daily revenue losses of over 6 million ISK and strongly criticizes the idea that Iceland has sufficient electricity, advocating for new power plant construction in the Westfjords.
items.why_matters: This article highlights critical issues with Iceland's energy infrastructure and supply, directly impacting businesses and sparking debate on national energy policy.

items.title: Sýna ekki vilja að slá á verðbólgu og hækka álagningu, segir FÍB
items.summary: The Icelandic Automobile Association (FÍB) criticizes fuel companies for increasing markups, which they say contributes to inflation and shows no willingness to curb it. FÍB has called for real-time price transparency for all vehicle energy sellers and for the Consumer Agency to manage price comparisons.
